>> Mr. President,
ladies and gentlemen,
let us begin with the theme of today's
debate. Restoring trust, managing
transformation,
a united nations that delivers for all.
It is an interesting theme that allows
us for a very substantive discussion
which we have been witnessing for a week
now. Indeed, trust among states today is
at its lowest point since the cold war.
The necessary reforms are stalling.
More and more voices are saying that the
UN is not working in the interests of
all and is incapable of managing change.
This is largely because we the member
states have in large part become mired
in endless debates but have failed to
give the organization a real opportunity
to act. That is precisely why the theme
of this session sounds today like a
verdict on our collective indecision and
at the same time as a diagnosis calling
for urgent treatment. We are surrounded
by a systemic crisis in international
relations. We see this everywhere. The
air is thick with anxiety from Europe to
the Middle East, from Asia to Africa and
Latin America.
Wars and conflicts are engulfing the
world. They are claiming lives, tearing
families apart.
turning thriving cities into ruins and
giving rise to ever more waves of mass
forced migration.
Global supply chains are being

alarming sign is the collapse of the
system of strategic stability. For the
first time since the 1970s, there are no

strategic arms between the major nuclear
powers. There are no treaties, no
verification mechanisms, and no
predictability.
Humanity is once again teetering on the
brink of existence. That is a brink that
we had hoped we had left for good in the
last century. How did we reach this
point? Well, it is no mere coincidence.
It is the inevitable result of actions
by certain states aimed at deliberately
undermining the system of international
relations so that the world would
develop not according to the laws of
peaceful coexistence but rather the
principle of might makes right and
political selfishness. If we truly want
to restore trust, we must not hide
behind diplomatic nicities, but honestly
identify the causes of crisis. In 1945
in San Francisco at the UN founding
conference, US President Harry Truman
spoke words that today sound like a
prophecy.
No matter how great our strength, we
must deny ourselves the license to do
always as we please.
If all those with great power had acted
as Truman said, we would have avoided
many wars and conflicts. Unfortunately,
however, the desire to live at the
expense of others has remained the
dominant narrative in the collective
west's development. During the Cold War,
the balance of power was maintained by a
system of checks and balances between
the two opposing political systems. But
since the 1990s, when that balance
collapsed, the policy of unrestrained
superiority has begun to grow rapidly.
And in recent years, this policy has
reached its peak. Western countries have
effectively trampled on international
law and started to force everyone to act
according to so-called rules, destroying
unwelcome countries and suppressing
unbounded peoples. And these rules are
like traffic signs in a city that they

have a green light while everyone else
faces strict restrictions. But this

Western interest. Now, let's add to that
unfair global trade where the rules are
written to serve the interests of
transnational corporations and also
illegal unilateral sanctions that are
suffocating entire nations. And those
efforts are intensifying. But what is
the UN doing? The organization has not
been able to resolve a single serious
conflict. Its role has instead boiled

appeals to those who have already
suffered and that of is of course
leading to further escalation. The
leadership of the European Union is

unbralled desire to preserve their
slipping hedgemony and they're

and the maintenance of peace. And to
achieve this, they are prepared to
sacrifice even the well-being of their
own citizens.

they don't. Do they want to be cannon

Nevertheless, in the West,

quote unquote discovered it 150 years

is that if not identity theft? Western
elites do not like the new multipolar

to to exploit instability. In Bellarus,
we see this most clearly in the example

neocolonialism and putting aside the

um it is fairly justified the very fact

China's project this confirms that the

that is why new formats of cooperation

But we in Belarus do not see them as

have a recipe for restoring the UN to
its intended purpose. And it's very
simple. Individual countries must stop
using the organization, our shared
organization, for their own selfish
ends. And they must begin to think about
the fate of our planet, our shared
planet as a whole. Only then will the
theme of this session cease to be a
romantic wish and instead become a real
program of action.
Concrete structural steps are also
necessary. First reform of the UN
security council. This body cannot
remain in a form that was appropriate
for the midentth century. The council
must be strengthened by expanding the
category of permanent members to include
the countries of the south which today
play an everinccreasing role in world
affairs. The voice of the global
majority must be heard loud and clear in
the security council. Second, restoring
respect for international law and the UN
charter and specifically respect for the
law, not the rules-based order. The UN
charter has been and remains the only
universal document that recognizes the
sovereign equality of all states. Third,
reform of specialized UN agencies. First
and foremost, the international
financial institutions, the World Bank,
the International Monetary Fund, the
International Finance Corporation, the
World Trade Organization, they must
become fair, transparent, accountable,
and focused on their mandates. Voting
quotas in financial institutions must
reflect the demographic and economic
realities of the 21st century rather
than the post-war balance of power. The
use of these organizations for political
purposes must be nipped in the bud. This
also applies to the International Labor
Organization. One might think its
mission is to promote social dialogue.
However, today the ILO in the finest
traditions of the Communist
International is attempting to cultivate
revolutionary forces in some countries
out of labor unions and not to protect
workers rights, but to destabilize the
situation in countries that are pursuing
independent policies at the behest of
certain other countries. And most
importantly, with each new crisis,
ordinary people around the world are
asking themselves, why isn't the UN
working to establish peace? People
aren't interested in the UN's
constraints. They want to see action and
results, and there are none. It is
therefore no surprise that many equate
the work of our organization with its
secretariat, which is dominated by
representatives of Western countries.
And just like in Brussels, this is a
world of comfortable offices, of
sky-high salaries, and a lifestyle that
is very far removed from the concerns of
those in need of assistance in various
corners of our planet. Many of those
officials have never even been to the
conflict zones and they are much further
away from them than any volunteer on the
front lines. And this is of course not
so much a criticism of the secretariat
rather it is a criticism of us the
member states who have allowed this to
become the norm who have allowed this to
happen. The Republic of Belarus is a
founding member of the United Nations.
We were there at the very beginning of
the organization in 1945 and so it pains
us to see the weakening of the UN.
Therefore we offer constructive
criticism of the organization hoping
that it can recover and take on a new
lease on life. We are convinced that the
UN must remain the primary universal
forum for addressing common challenges.
In these circumstances, Belarus is
making its contribution to creating a
new world. First of all, on food
security. We are developing successfully
and making a significant contribution to
global food security. Belarus remains a
reliable supplier of fertilizers,
highquality food, meat, dairy products,
and grain to countries in Africa, Asia,
and Latin America. and we are doing this
despite the lo logistical barriers,
financial restrictions and transport
blockades imposed by the European Union.
Uh second, our role in peace. Belarus
has always been and remains a country of
peace. We've proven our ability to serve
as a reliable platform for negotiations
and we're ready to continue doing
everything possible to achieve peace in
Ukraine as soon as possible. But let's
be frank, any lasting peace in that
country is not possible without
addressing the root causes which have
been ignored for years. These include
plans to bring Ukraine into NATO
contrary to all security realities. The
failure to implement the Minsk
agreements which were the only
legitimate path to peace. And let me
remind you that the implementation of
these agreements was sabotaged in order
to buy time and allow Ukraine to rearm
and that has been acknowledged by by
Western politicians very recently. The
endless supply of weapons to Ukraine
will only lead to the destruction of
Ukraine itself and its people. We call
for the prompt beginning of genuine
negotiations that will lead to a lasting
peace. Third, the Eurasian security
architecture. Uh this is our particular
priority, ensuring Eurasian security. In
since 2023, we have successfully been
holding an international conference on
this in our capital where experts from
across Eurasia discuss ways to solve our
continent's problems. We are
successfully promoting the idea of
drafting a Eurasian charter on diversity
and multipolarity in the 21st century.
This initiative is part of an effort to
create a new architecture of equal and
indivisible security on our vast
continent stretching from the Atlantic
to the Pacific.
Finally, our openness to dialogue. We
are ready to cooperate with all
interested countries. We also are
leaving the door open to those western
pol politicians who are genuinely ready
for a dialogue of equals. But there are
things that are unacceptable for us.
Pressure, dictates, ultimatums and
illegal sanctions. Mr. President, the
uniolar world, as we can see, is
sinking. Western elites are accustomed
to dominance and they are trying to keep
it afloat. But in their futile efforts,
they are only sewing chaos. We've spoken
about this alarming trend last year as
well, calling for action. But we see
that nothing is changing and it's only
getting worse. Therefore, Belarus and
the countries of the global majority do
not wish to to go down with the wreckage
of this ship and we are choosing a
different path. We are building a
multipolar and just world of equal
states in the interests of all of our
peoples. We have no other choice. Thank
you for your attention.
I thank the Minister of Foreign Affairs
of Bellarus.
